subject: Biotechnology
title: Clopidogrel and CYP2C19
description: A 60-second lesson on Clopidogrel and CYP2C19.

hook.text: Clopidogrel prevents heart attacks — but one in three patients cannot activate it. Their CYP2C19 gene is the reason.

buildup.text: Clopidogrel is a prodrug requiring CYP2C19 activation — loss-of-function variants leave the drug inactive.

discovery.text: Poor metabolizers have 40% higher risk of stent thrombosis — the drug meant to protect them does not work.

twist.text: Alternative drugs like ticagrelor do not need CYP2C19 activation — but they cost more and cause more bleeding.

climax.text: Preemptive pharmacogenomic testing at Mount Sinai saves $1,500 per patient by avoiding ineffective clopidogrel prescriptions.

punchline.text: Test the gene, choose the drug — CYP2C19 testing saves hearts and money.

quiz.question: Why doesn't clopidogrel work in some patients?
options: Their blood is naturally resistant to all anti-clotting drugs
CYP2C19 loss-of-function variants prevent activation of the prodrug into its active form
Their stents are made of a material that blocks clopidogrel absorption
